previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, atrial fibrillation, and a history of mitral regurgitation was admitted after waking with severe shortness of breath. She was found to have acute hypoxemic respiratory failure due to volume overload and pulmonary edema. She was stabilized with CPAP and nitroglycerin, and underwent urgent hemodialysis, which improved her symptoms. Repeat imaging showed resolution of pulmonary edema. A lung opacity was deemed more likely asymmetric edema than infection, and antibiotics were discontinued. An echocardiogram revealed worsening mitral regurgitation and pulmonary hypertension, prompting a cardiology follow-up. She had a transient episode of atrial fibrillation during dialysis but remained stable. A known pancreatic cyst was noted, with plans for repeat imaging in six months. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up plans for sleep study, cardiology, and dialysis management.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:  ___ female with history of ESRD secondary

localizing symptoms, she reported some sore throat, dry cough in 
addition to a concerning complaint of new graft tenderness.  
Imaging demonstrated ""slightly increased stranding around the 
failed right lower quadrant renal transplant may reflect 
continued rejection post-embolization degeneration, however, 
underlying infection cannot be excluded. There are no 
neighboring fluid collections or abscesses.""  She has a history

Admission chest x-ray is at baseline.  While here, blood, urine,

were pending at discharge.  She was initially treated with 
linezolid, levofloxacin, and flagyl in the ED but was not 
continued on antibiotics initially given lack of source.  She 
spiked overnight on ___hest was ordered which 
demonstrated possible infectious process in RLL so she was 
started on levofloxacin 250mg daily for a 14 day course (last 
day ___.  ID was consulted and recommended a viral and 
fungal work-up, which was either negative or pending as 
discharge.  Blood cultures all with no growth at discharge (none 
were finalized).  She underwent a TTE on ___, which did not 
show any vegetations.  Her fever curve downtrended and by 
discharge, she was afebrile for > 24 hours.  Likely, this was 
secondary to a viral process.  She is aware to monitor her 
symptoms and to contact her PCP or go to the emergency 
department with any concerns.  
  
# Atrial fibrillation:  Patient went into a-fib with RVR in ED, 
which responded well to 500 cc NS and metoprolol 12.5mg PO x 1.  
She never experienced any chest pain, palpitations, dizziness or 
lightheadedness.  We continued home coumadin at 3mg daily.  She 
was also continued on amiodarone 200mg daily and metoprolol 
12.5mg PO BID.  
  
# ESRD ___ PCKD s/p failed transplant, now on HD: She gets 
dialyzed on ___ at ___.  She was dialyzed 
here and tolerated it well.  Transplant surgery followed given 
possible indication for transplant nephrectomy in the setting of 
low grade rejection.  It was determined that nephrectomy was not 
indicated at this time.   She was continued on home nephrocaps, 
sevelamer and midodrine with HD.  
  
# Hypocalcemia: Found to be very hypocalcemic (6.0) on 
admission.  She also reported symptoms of paresthesias in hand 
and numbness around lips.  Ionized Ca 0.96 on admission. Her QTc 
was noted to be lengthening - 464 ___, 452 in ___ and 443 in 
___.  Hypocalcemia was thought to be secondary to cinacalcet 
for secondary hyperPTH.  PTH level returned at elevated to 323.  
She was given calcium carbonate 1500mg x 1, calcium gluconate 
2gm x 1 and kept on calcium carbonate 500mg TID with improvement 
in her calcium.  On discharge, calcium was 8.1 so his dose of 
calcium carbonate was increased to 750mg TID and we continued to 
hold his cinacalcet.  We ask his nephrologist to determine when 
and if to resume the cincalcet.
  
# Hypothyroidism: continued home levothyroxine at 75mcg daily  
  
# BRBPR: sounds like hemorrhoidal bleeding and was isolated 
event with no other during her hospitalization.  Hct stable 
throughout admission.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Status post renal transplant with fever, tachycardia,
assess for pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  Single frontal view of the chest was provided.  As compared with
multiple prior exams, the appearance of the chest is stable with vague basilar
opacities, likely representing scarring or atelectasis.  The possibility of
pneumonia is difficult to exclude though given the stability over time,
chronic scarring or atelectasis is favored.  No large effusion is seen, though
the CP angles are partially excluded bilaterally.  Heart size is top normal. 
Mediastinal contour normal.  Tracheobronchial tree calcification noted.  Clips
to the right of the upper trachea in the superior mediastinum are likely from
prior thyroid resection.  Bony structures are intact.

IMPRESSION:  Stable exam without definite signs of pneumonia or CHF.  Lower
lung opacities are stable over time and likely represents scarring or chronic
atelectasis.

INDICATION:  ___ female status post renal transplant with fever and
tachycardia.

COMPARISON:  CT available from ___ and MR from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired 5 mm axial images of the abdomen and pelvis were
obtained following the uneventful administration of 130 cc of Omnipaque
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed at 5
mm slice thickness.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
Included views of the lung bases are clear.  There is no pericardial or
pleural effusion.  The heart size is top normal.  Severe mitral annulus
calcification is again seen (2:4).  The RCA is heavily calcified (2:4).  There
is no pericardial effusion.

Again seen are innumerable cystic hepatic lesions, some calcified, the largest
at the right hepatic dome measuring 7.7 cm in diameter (2:8), compatible with
known history of polycystic kidney disease.  No new lesions are detected. 
Cholelithiasis is again seen.  The gallbladder wall is chronically thickened
(2:27); however, there is no neighboring stranding to suggest acute
cholecystitis.  The spleen is top normal in size.  A hypoenhancing anterior
4.0 x 2.5 cm lesion (2:28) is unchanged, likely reflecting small collection of
cysts or a small hemangioma.  The pancreas, stomach, and intra-abdominal loops
of small and large bowel are normal.  The native kidneys are resected. 
Numerous paraaortic and retroperitoneal lymph nodes (2:28) are unchanged from
the prior examination.  There is no free air or free fluid.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  
The rectum, sigmoid colon, and intrapelvic loops of small and large bowel are
normal.

Again seen is a right lower quadrant transplanted kidney, with no discernable
corticomedullary junction (2:55), reflecting rejection.  Arterial embolization
coils are unchanged in position (2:55).  Neighboring stranding has slightly
increased since the ___ examination, likely secondary to continued
rejection and post-embolization degeneration, although superimposed infection
cannot be excluded.  There are no neighboring fluid collections or abscesses. 
The grafted ureter appears thickened, and terminates within the bladder, which
is collapsed with neighboring stranding (2:71).  Infection in this regions
also cannot be excluded.  There is no intrapelvic free fluid or
lymphadenopathy.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  
Mild dextroscoliosis of the lumbar spine is again seen (601b:39), with
associated moderate multilevel degenerative changes, including disc height
loss from L1 through S1, with associated endplate sclerosis and extensive
anterior and posterior osteophytosis.  There is mild thecal sac narrowing. 
Grade 1 retrolisthesis of L3 over L4 (602b:41) appears stable.  There are no
bony lesions concerning for infection or malignancy.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Slightly increased stranding around the failed right lower quadrant renal
transplant may reflect continued rejection post-embolization degeneration,
however, underlying infection cannot be excluded.  There are no neighboring
fluid collections or abscesses.
2.  Continued stranding around the bladder may reflect a UTI. Correlate with
urinlaysis.
3.  Numerous hepatic cysts are unchanged.
4.  Chronically thickened gallbladder wall, with no CT evidence for acute
cholecystitis.

CT CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Fever, patient with renal transplant.

Comparison is made with prior studies, CT abdomen, ___, and chest x-ray,
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT through the chest was acquired without IV
contrast.  5, 1.25 mm collimation images, sagittal and coronal reformations
were provided and reviewed.

FINDINGS: There are few calcified granulomas.  There are multiple soft tissue
and ground-glass lung nodules.  All of the soft tissue lung nodules measure
less than 3 mm.  The largest ground-glass opacity is located in the right
upper lobe measuring 10 mm (4, 62).  An ill-defined branching opacity in the
right lower lobe could be a bronchial impaction (4, 140).

The airways are patent to the subsegmental level.  Patient is status post
right thyroidectomy.  There are small hypodense rounded areas in the left lobe
of the thyroid that should be correlated with ultrasound.  There are no
enlarged mediastinal, hilar, or axillary lymph nodes.  The main pulmonary
arteries are enlarged suggesting pulmonary hypertension.  All the coronary
arteries have atheromatous calcifications.  There is calcification in the
mitral annulus.  Calcification in the aortic valve is of unknown hemodynamic
significance.  Cardiac size is top normal.  There is no pleural or pericardial
effusion.

This examination is not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation.  Please
refer to complete abdomen CT from ___ for more details.

There are no bone findings of malignancy.

IMPRESSION:  Findings most likely consistent with an infectious process; could
be viral, fungal.

Soft tissue nodules that are small, some calcified and non-calcified, could be
calcified and non-calcified granulomas.

Coronary calcifications.

Calcification in the mitral annulus and aortic valve.  

Findings suggestive of pulmonary hypertension.

For all the abdominal findings, please refer to the prior abdomen CT from
___.
